definition: Despite similar-sounding names, natural gas (C1, methane, the lightest hydrocarbon) and natural gasoline (C5+, heavier hydrocarbons resembling low-octane naphtha) are very different substances.
core_idea: The 'C1 vs C5+' framing is used to head off confusion between methane-based natural gas and the pentane-plus product called natural gasoline.
key_points: C1 = methane = natural gas, the lightest hydrocarbon gas.
C5+ = natural gasoline = heavier hydrocarbons, similar to low-octane naphtha.
relationships: Natural gasoline is the pentanes-plus fraction of NGLs, distinct from methane-based natural gas
caveats: The similarity in names ('natural gas' vs 'natural gasoline') invites confusion despite the substances being chemically very different.
